comparison: Both address model architecture and plasticity rules (C5, C6, C18, C33, C34, C36). OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED with clear mathematical formulations and internal consistency. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, expressing concerns about 'semi-heuristic' derivations and 'unclear aspects to the formal derivation,' specifically noting equation 13 may be incomplete/incorrect.

Both evaluate the core finding that spontaneous activity replicates learned transition statistics (C7, C20, C21, C47-C49, C54, C64, C65, C107). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative alignment across multiple figures; peer reviewers praise this as 'an important contribution' with 'comprehensive simulations.'

Both address necessity of inhibitory plasticity (C71-C73, C108, C110, C111). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval demonstrates necessity through ablation studies showing blurred assemblies without inhibitory plasticity. Peer reviewers highlight 'the interplay between excitation and inhibition' as 'a highlight of the study.'

Both evaluate weight structure mechanisms (C66-C70, C121). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of within-assembly strengthening and between-assembly encoding. Peer reviewers accept these mechanistic findings as contributing to understanding how the model encodes transition statistics.

Both address task switching capability (C74-C80). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval demonstrates reorganization of between-assembly connections with stable within-assembly connections. Peer reviewers view this positively as 'a good-to-know type of result that is not very common in sequence learning papers.'

Both evaluate comparison to songbird data (C8, C23, C97-C102, C105, C139, C140). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting the comparison is limited to one phenomenon and doesn't establish the mechanism is actually used by the brain. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging 'finches are classical model animals' and the comparison strengthens biological plausibility.

Both address timescale differences in plasticity (C42-C45). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these differences are consistent with experimental data (D'amour and Froemke, 2015). Peer reviewers do not raise concerns, accepting this as emerging naturally from the model architecture.

Both evaluate learning of temporal community structure (C81-C83, C85-C87, C89, C90, C92-C94). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of community structure learning, PCA clustering, and within-community transition speeds. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings as demonstrating the model scales to complex tasks.

Both address robustness to parameter variations (C55-C60). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, showing robustness across multiple parameter variations. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED after initially raising concerns about constant background input; authors addressed this with additional simulations showing robustness to varied inputs.

Partial overlap on model assumptions (C61-C63 in OpenEval; C32, C38, C61-C63 in peer). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting performance degrades under extreme conditions. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, identifying assumptions about plastic synapses and equal neuron numbers as weaknesses requiring validation, though authors' additional simulations 'strengthened the paper significantly.'

Both address model limitations regarding Markovian transitions (C146-C150). Both rate SUPPORTED (OpenEval) and SUPPORTED (peer). OpenEval notes limitations are acknowledged with reasonable speculation about working memory solutions. Peer reviewers explicitly appreciate the transparent discussion of limitations in the manuscript.

OpenEval evaluates scalability to complex tasks (C81-C83) as SUPPORTED with detailed evidence from Figure 4. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these claims in isolation.

OpenEval evaluates distinctions from prior approaches (C112-C120, C133-C138) as SUPPORTED, noting clear conceptual differences from Hebbian learning and prior computational models. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these comparative claims.

OpenEval rates speculation about biological implementation and RL advantages (C122-C132) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are reasonable but untested hypotheses. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these speculative claims.
OpenEval evaluates background context claims (C1, C2, C10-C17) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these introductory/background claims.
OpenEval evaluates gap identification and how current study addresses it (C3, C4, C25, C109) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these framing claims.

OpenEval rates broad interpretive statements about implications (C8, C9, C24, C152, C153) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation beyond what is directly demonstrated. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these interpretive claims, though peer R4 touches on C8.
